name: pair_device
description: Add/pair or remove a physical device -- callable any time, including mid-Plan-session. Ask the customer what protocol (insteon, z-wave, zigbee, matter, x10) if unclear. insteon/zwave/zigbee/matter are wired up; x10 returns a not-yet-supported message -- walk the customer through manual pairing instead. A Z-Wave controller still running the Legacy (pre-Z-Matter) generation returns a clear error for any zwave action -- tell the customer to use the ISY administrative console for that controller. IMPORTANT for adding a zwave/zigbee/matter device: there is no such thing as a customer-readable device address for these protocols, and add_by_address is not a valid action for them at all (see _PROTOCOL_ACTIONS). Once the customer says they want to add a device of one of these protocols, protocol is the only thing this call needs -- call start_inclusion immediately, in this same turn, with no clarifying question of any kind first. This means: never ask whether they know the device's address (not even rhetorically, e.g. 'you probably don't have an address, right?'); never present 'address vs. pairing mode' as a choice; and never ask for device_type either -- it's optional, so just omit it unless the customer already volunteered it unprompted. Do not make the customer confirm anything before you open the pairing window -- open it, then tell them to activate the device. Asking any question here before calling start_inclusion is exactly the fabrication/stalling pattern to avoid: there is nothing to clarify. Action depends on protocol: add_by_address (insteon/x10 only -- these are the only protocols with a customer-readable address in this system) is for a device whose own address the customer already knows or can read off the unit -- this call itself waits (up to ~80s) for the new device to actually become usable before returning, so it's safe to reference the returned device_address in the very next tool call. start_inclusion/finish_inclusion (insteon/zwave/zigbee/matter) is for adding everything else -- start_inclusion puts the controller in pairing mode so the customer can activate one or more devices, finish_inclusion then commits everything included during that window and waits the same way, returning whatever was newly discovered directly in its own result's new_devices list (address + whatever name the hub assigned, usually blank -- no separate lookup needed to find or name them). start_exclusion/finish_exclusion (zwave/zigbee/matter only -- insteon has no distinct hardware remove mode here) is for removing a device that's already known, so BOTH actions require device_address (the exact address from DEVICE DATABASE for the device the customer named -- resolve it there first, never guess). The two protocol groups behave differently here, and this matters for how you talk to the customer: for zwave, this is a real two-step activation window just like start_inclusion/finish_inclusion -- start_exclusion puts the controller in removal mode and echoes device_address back to you in its result, tell the customer to physically activate the device now, then call finish_exclusion with that same device_address once they confirm (finish_exclusion waits, up to ~80s, specifically for that address to disappear from the device list, and reports it in removed_devices). For zigbee/matter, there is no activation window at all -- either start_exclusion or finish_exclusion by itself performs the ENTIRE removal immediately and returns status=exclusion_committed with removed_devices already populated; do not tell the customer to activate/press anything on the device, do not wait for them to confirm, and do not call the other action afterward -- one call is the whole operation, done. For adding a marketplace plugin (not a physical device), use install_plugin/buy_plugin instead -- that's a different kind of entity with its own link space (/plugins/...). A physical device this tool adds/pairs/removes, regardless of protocol, is a device node: when you mention it in your reply, link it as /nodes/{address} per UI NAVIGATION RULES (using the address this tool's own result just gave you, e.g. new_devices[].address) -- never a /plugins/... link, that's only ever for the plugin marketplace/dashboard/licenses, not for a device a plugin happens to have created either. When the customer names a specific device to remove, never guess its protocol from the device's name/model to pick this call's protocol argument -- that's a fabrication risk identical to stating the protocol out loud. Either call get_device_family (via get_diagnostics_prompt/run_diagnostic_step) first, or just try node_op(delete, node_id=...): it succeeds directly for insteon, and for zwave/zigbee/matter/plugin it's rejected with the device's real protocol/flow named in the error, so you never have to guess which protocol to pass here.

action.description: add_by_address is insteon/x10 ONLY (needs device_address) -- not a valid action for zwave/zigbee/matter, which have no customer-readable address before inclusion; use start_inclusion for those instead, never ask the customer for an address. start_inclusion/finish_inclusion (add) work for insteon/zwave/zigbee/matter (finish_inclusion optionally takes flag). start_exclusion/finish_exclusion (remove) work for zwave/zigbee/matter only and both require device_address -- for zwave this is a real two-step activation window (finish_exclusion optionally takes flag); for zigbee/matter there is no window at all and either action alone performs the whole removal immediately, no second call needed.

device_address.description: The device's own physical address, exactly as shown in DEVICE DATABASE. Required for action=add_by_address (a device you're adding) and for action=start_exclusion/finish_exclusion (an existing device you're removing -- pass the same value to both calls).

device_type.description: Optional device-type hint (add_by_address/start_inclusion). Never ask the customer for this before calling -- omit it unless they already mentioned the device type unprompted; it is not worth delaying the call for.

flag.description: Optional numeric flag for finish_inclusion/finish_exclusion (defaults to 1). Insteon-specific -- ignored for zwave/zigbee/matter.
